about: scripts/perf-guard.py: the compiler, built in release mode from the checkout, compiling the frozen input (its sources at input_revision, the same for every checkout). Measured on Linux x86-64; scripts/perf-guard.py --update writes the metrics that improved beyond their tolerance, --raise=METRIC=REASON one that is higher on purpose with its reason (raise_reason), in the commit that moves it, and move input_revision only with a re-baseline. Tolerances are fractions of the value (tolerance) or counts (tolerance_abs).

allocated_bytes.why: Deterministic for a given source tree; the slack absorbs ordinary code growth between deliberate updates.
allocated_bytes.raise_reason: the frozen input moved from b3a22d6bf to 4df7d3229, whose stdlib declares intrinsics as bodyless externs (the old input's stub bodies are E1021): the larger compiler of that revision, measured on it; on the old input the compiler change was within tolerance of every metric

collections.why: Phase-end collections (CompileOptions.phaseCollections) plus the byte trigger as a safety net; one extra collection can come from crossing a trigger boundary.

live_bytes_tables.why: Live data at the end of the phase, from a heap census there: deterministic to a fraction of a megabyte for a given source tree; the slack absorbs ordinary code growth.
